raw_response:
I am old now, 68, and only one person is working this 2 mu, so I cannot do fancy things. I farm the same wheat-maize rotation as around here because it is steady. Wheat gives me grain first, then maize follows right after harvest, and that way even if one side is not so good, I still have the other. I do mostly what has worked on my land. If I change too much at my age and it goes wrong, I have no one to cover the loss.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, around the usual village time. I will use the common seed I can buy nearby, not some expensive new one. Before sowing I will put a base fertilizer, not too little, because if wheat seedlings come up weak it is hard to fix later. If the wheat looks yellow after winter, I will topdress once more and then water with the well. Water costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times, but wheat here usually still needs a few turns. For maize, I will plant as soon as wheat is cut, no delay, because the summer season is tight. I will keep it simple, quick tillage and sowing, use hybrid maize seed like most people do now, put one base dose and one chasing dose. If rain is decent, I water less; if it stays dry, I will give one or two irrigations from the well. I do not want to save too much on fertilizer and lose yield, but with only 2 mu I also watch every yuan.
